title: Accordion Scheduler: stochastic latency reserves and proportional fairness for prefill/decode
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: In mixed workloads our current prefill/decode scheduler oscillates between latency-first and throughput-first modes, resulting in either p99 latency regressions for interactive tenants or wasted GPU cycles for batch tenants. We need a scheduling policy that can gracefully allocate small, stochastic latency reserves to latency-sensitive requests while still aggregating work for throughput when headroom exists.

Proposal: Implement an "Accordion Scheduler" that maintains a per-tenant stochastic latency reserve (a soft budget) and exposes proportional fairness across tenants when reserves are exhausted. Key ideas:
- Soft latency reserves: each tenant has a small probabilistic reserve expressed as token-time budget derived from historical p95/p99 usage. Reserves allow micro-slices to be hedged without forcing full low-latency paths for every request.
- Accordion splitting: dynamically split prefill/decode phases into variable-width micro-slices according to reserve state and current kernel-cost estimate. When reserves are available, prefer narrower slices to reduce p99; when exhausted, expand slices to increase batching.
- Kernel-aware gating: use kernel selection hints (fast kernels vs. quantized slower kernels) from the kernel probe router to decide when to favor slicing vs. aggregation so we don't overload kernels with many tiny launches.
- Attention-cost feedback: integrate a lightweight attention-cost estimator (tokens*avg-attn-density) to bias the split width so heavy-attention requests are batched more aggressively.

Goals: reduce p99 for interactive tenants by >=15% on mixed workloads while keeping throughput loss <8% on benchmarked batch traces. Provide config toggles for strict-latency vs. economy mode and safe fallbacks that degrade to current allocator under stress.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows >=15% p99 improvement for latency-sensitive tenants on 60/40 mixed trace with throughput loss <8%
End-to-end canary on staging with fixed canary tenants demonstrates stable p95 and no increase in OOMs or kernel launch errors
Kernel probe telemetry shows no >10% increase in small-launch overhead compared to baseline
Console exposes per-tenant reserve utilization and an opt-in flag for tenants to prioritize latency (runtime-1.24 rollout)
tasks: Design doc and cost model: publish to Confluence and share with runtime and kernel teams
Simulator implementation: extend existing prefill-decode simulator to support stochastic reserves and attention-cost estimator
Runtime implementation: accordion-phase splitter, reserve allocator, and kernel-hint integration
Observability: add telemetry for reserve levels, split widths, kernel launch counts, and per-tenant p99 measurements
Canary rollout: staging -> limited-prod canary -> ramp based on SLO and kernel telemetry
Post-mortem hooks: automatic rollback thresholds and a playbook entry
comments: 2026-02-12 - Maya Patel: Initial design doc uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Accordion+Scheduler+Proposal (see section 'reserve derivation'). Added cost model spreadsheet: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1abc-accordion-costs

2026-02-18 - Samir Gupta: Ran first simulator sweep against historical mixed trace (60% interactive, 40% batch). Findings: aggressive reserves improved latency p99 by ~22% but throughput dropped ~12% when split width was fixed at 4 tokens. Need kernel-aware gating to cut small-launch overhead.

2026-02-20 - Diego Ramirez (kernel eng): Suggested adding a fast-path kernel hint so scheduler can avoid using tiny slices on kernels with high launch overhead. Refer to PR that adds kernel hint API: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kernels/pull/874

2026-02-23 - Samir Gupta: Implemented attention-cost estimator prototype in simulator. When biasing splits by attention-density, throughput loss dropped to 7% with p99 improvement of 16%. Saved simulator logs: gs://redwood-sim/accordion/2026-02-23/logs.tar.gz

2026-02-26 - Maya Patel: Discussion in runtime sync about fairness knob. We will implement proportional fairness with a tunable alpha parameter and a short-term decay window to avoid oscillation across tenants.

2026-02-28 - Samir Gupta: Branch created for runtime changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/compare/accordion-scheduler (WIP). Added feature flag runtime.accordion.enabled and per-tenant config runtime.accordion.reserve_pct

2026-03-01 - QA: Started unit tests for reserve accounting and split scheduler. Found race when multiple micro-slices from same prefill are enqueued; added a short mutex around slice-creation as mitigation. Opened follow-up ENG-415679 to investigate high-contention optimization.
notes: Trade-offs considered: tight latency reserves reduce p99 but increase kernel-launch overhead and reduce batching efficiency; attention-weighted grouping recovers much of the throughput by avoiding splitting heavy attention inputs.
Rollout plan: start with conservative reserve_pct=0.05 for all tenants, enable per-tenant opt-in for strict-latency, monitor kernel-launch p50/p95, and enable kernel hint gating as canary progresses.

Related work: ENG-271828 (congestion controller) provides admission signals that the Accordion Scheduler will consume to avoid overload; ENG-142558 (kernel probe router) provides kernel-cost hints. Coordinate API changes with those teams.
